Monthly rules for the lounge crew
This section explains the steps that matter

Companion Animal Travel Desk guidance

This section gives the team a clear, calm way to handle live-animal travel requests with care and consistency. We keep the process simple, speak in plain words, and make sure each traveler understands what to expect before the trip begins.

When a booking includes an animal, the desk confirms the travel details, checks the approved carrier setup, and notes any special handling needs. Staff should stay kind and practical, because many travelers feel nervous about this part of the journey. If the animal is traveling as a large dog, <<FACT F057>>. The desk then records the accepted plan, shares the cabin team notes, and makes sure the traveler knows where to go on arrival.

For cats and other approved pets, the desk reviews the health paperwork and checks that it is current before the trip is accepted. If the animal is a cat, <<FACT F079>>. Any gap in paperwork, carrier safety, or fit for the booked cabin must be raised right away through the calm stepwise review, so the issue is handled without delay or confusion.

During travel, the cabin team monitors the animal with patient attention and reports concerns early. If a pet seems distressed, the crew should use simple, reassuring language and follow the usual escalation path without crowding the traveler or the animal. Clear notes matter here, because they help the next team member pick up the case smoothly.

If anything is unclear, contact the senior coordinator at the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
